input.quote: (c) subject to Section 12.10.2 and Section 12.7 (solely following the License Option Exercise Closing Date), AbbVie shall cease any and all Exploitation of Licensed Compounds and Licensed Products and transfer to Harpoon, or destroy (at Harpoon's sole election), copies of all data and Information generated by AbbVie in connection with the Exploitation of Licensed Compounds or Licensed Products, and all rights in such Licensed Compounds and Licensed Products shall revert back to Harpoon
input.rationale: This is a development/option and licence agreement, not a hosting or services arrangement, and Article 12 already contains a developed exit architecture: Sections 12.6–12.8 govern effects of termination and reversion (transfer of data, Information and Regulatory Documentation, reversion licences, and Harpoon-requested assistance under 12.7.3 and 12.7.8), Section 12.10.2 gives AbbVie a wind-down/sell-off period for inventory after termination, and Section 12.5.2 entitles the non-debtor Party (potentially us) to a complete duplicate of, or access to, all licensed Intellectual Property and its embodiments in a bankruptcy. Directionally, the data-transfer and transition-assistance obligations on termination run against our party (AbbVie transfers or destroys data at Harpoon's election and provides reversion assistance for Harpoon Reversion Products); Harpoon holds no "Customer Data" of ours requiring return, and our inbound transition rights (IND transition under Section 3, and the Manufacturing Technology Transfer with reasonable assistance under Sections 4.5.2–4.5.3) are already secured during the Term. The purpose of the rule — orderly exit with data and continuity — is therefore met, at or around the fallback level; the only sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a fixed six-month assistance window and a written deletion certification) are noted here rather than flagged, since inserting a mirror data-return duty on Harpoon would add nothing for us and could invite reciprocal tightening of our own reversion obligations.
